quotes: Active: Syndra propels a wave of force in a cone in the target direction that deals magic damage to enemies hit and knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra based on proximity, though not through terrain.

Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units and up to 1200 units away from Syndra based on proximity, knocking back enemies they hit over 70 units, though not through terrain. Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds, during which they are also revealed, and dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast.

Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 80 Splinters of Wrath enhances Scatter the Weak to have an increased scatter angle and slow enemies hit by 70% for 1.25 seconds starting after the knock back ends or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended.
step_1_what_cc_does_syndra_E_apply.conclusion: Syndra E applies exactly three crowd-control kinds: knockback (400-800 units, base cast), stun (1.25 s, sphere-knockback branch), and, at 80 Splinters, a 70% slow for 1.25 s. There is no CC kind on E called 'cc_kind'.

step_2_cc_taxonomy_check.quote_stun: Stun - Full disable: cannot move, attack, cast, or activate items for the duration; interrupts channels and attack windups; reduced by tenacity.
step_2_cc_taxonomy_check.quote_airborne: Airborne - Forced-displacement crowd control: the unit is flung in a direction (knock up/back/aside/pull) and cannot move, attack, or cast for the duration; tenacity does not affect it.
step_2_cc_taxonomy_check.conclusion: The full cached CC atom taxonomy contains no atom named 'cc_kind'. 'cc_kind' is therefore not a crowd-control kind at all.

step_5_is_the_ordering_claim_itself_supp.analysis: R is Unit-targeted (point-and-click) and therefore cannot be 'missed'; it needs no CC to land, and E's base effect pushes the target 400-800 units directly AWAY from Syndra, i.e. toward or past R's range edge. The wiki-attested setup edge for R is sphere COUNT, not CC: R grabs up to 4 live spheres, and Q (7 s cooldown, spheres persist 6 s) plus W are what put live spheres on the ground. So 'E ... setup before R' is at best a weak generic CC-before-ultimate heuristic and is not the edge the cached data supports.
step_5_is_the_ordering_claim_itself_supp.conclusion: Even ignoring the placeholder token, the specific justification ('setup before R') is not derivable from the cached wiki text; the derivable pre-R setup is Q/W sphere placement.

verdict_rationale: New value is wrong: 'cc_kind' is an unsubstituted metadata field name, not a crowd-control kind - Syndra E's kinds per cached wiki text are knockback (400-800 units), stun (1.25 s via knocked-back Dark Spheres) and, at 80 Splinters, a 70% slow; and the 'setup before R' justification is itself unsupported since R is Unit-targeted while E displaces the target away from Syndra (the real pre-R setup is Q/W sphere count). Old value is also not correct: E demonstrably does apply crowd control, so the absence of any CC-setup source line left a genuine, wiki-attested signal unrecorded. The correct leaf would read '<slot> applies <actual atom> crowd control ...' with a real atom value (knockback / stun), which neither the old nor the new state contains.
